newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa's Telkom launches internet subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's Telkom launches internet subsidiary.

text.p: South Africa's state telecommunications utility, Telkom, said on Friday that it had launched a subsidiary to provide Internet-based services.

Telkom, which is expected to sell an equity stake of up to 30 percent to one of four foreign bidders shortly, said in a statement that the subsidiary Intekom (Pty) Ltd would "expose all South Africans to the full range of benefits the Internet has to offer, both as an information resource and as a business tool."

"Telkom will focus on making Internet connectivity equally accessible for all South Africans at the most affordable price," the statement said, adding that Telkom would also pioneer and stimulate use of Internet-based services by business.

"In its efforts to develop the industry in South Africa and eventually the entire continent, Intekom will enter into strategic relationships with national and international partners," the statement said. Intekom would be wholly owned by Telkom, but would operate as an independent unit," it said.
